text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel selector tweak last night we're seeing ~12% p99 tail regression on g4a and an uptick in GPU OOMs. Repro'd in perf-ci.

maria: Quick logs (from the failing job):
```
[2026-03-17T22:10:03Z] serve: selected kernel path=fast_matmul_q8 size=1024 seq=2048
[2026-03-17T22:10:03Z] cache: prefetch sampler hit=false key=prefix:abc123
[2026-03-17T22:10:03Z] kv: insert slot=437 frag=0.27 occupancy=0.78
[2026-03-17T22:10:03Z] oom: gpu0 out_of_memory while alloc tokens=512
```

adeel: Interesting — I think the probabilistic sampler we merged biases toward remote kernel variants for mid-length sequences. That plus the new kernel's per-request temp allocations could fragment GPU slab and cause LRU shadowing.

a deel: to be short -> sampler increased prefetch of low-hitrate prefixes, causing many single-use entries to populate LRU and push useful KV items out. (we saw similar in 1765432100-era experiments)

jun: I ran a quick profile on perf-ci-1995032101: overall kv hit-rate fell from 0.63 -> 0.49 for warm workloads post-change. Prefetch volume up 3.5x. Attached small table:
```
metric,baseline,after
kv_hitrate,0.63,0.49
prefetch_per_min,120,420
avg_slot_lifetime_s,3600,95
```

eva: avg_slot_lifetime dropping from 1h -> 95s screams single-use prefetches. That will show as fragmentation and create many tiny free slots that don't coalesce on GPU allocator.

maria: Do we have kernel allocation sizes? I suspect the new kernel uses a temporary buffer per beam which spikes allocator churn.

jun: yes — new kernel temp_buf ~24MB/request for our worst-case batch. Old kernel ~6MB. That aligns with fragmentation.

adeel: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert kernel selector to prefer old_matmul for seq<2048 OR reduce sampler prefetch probability by 0.7x. Quick heatmap suggested we only need to prefetch top-5 prefixes instead of top-20.

maria: Can we test sampler throttle first? rollback impacts rollout funnels.

eva: I'm +1 to throttle. Also propose changing eviction policy for GPU KV from pure LRU -> LRU-with-ghosting (track recent evicted keys for a few seconds) to avoid reinsert churn.

adeel: Implementation note: ghost list cheap memory (a few KB) and could reduce re-prefetch thrash.

ci-bot: perf-ci: run 1995032101 completed (maria@scheduler). diff vs baseline: p99 +11.9% , kv_hitrate -14pts.

jun: quick experiment plan (2-step):
1) sampler throttle x0.3 + prefetch cap 5 -> run perf-ci synthetic workload (low entropy) for 30m
2) if good, enable ghost list for 60m cluster test. collect slab fragmentation histograms, allocator free-run latency, kv occupancy and hit-rate.

maria: I spun up a canary with sampler throttle + prefetch cap 5 on g4a-spot pool. Early metrics: p99 back down ~4% (half the regression) and kv_hitrate recovered to 0.58.

eva: Good. For step 2 I can prototype ghosting on dev branch. Need approval to push to canary for 1h.

adeel: Approve from my side. Also let's add a short TTL on single-use prefixes (if seen <2 hits within first 2m, set ttl=30s) — cheap heuristic to drop one-offs quickly.

jun: I'll add instrumentation hooks for kernel allocator peak, slot fragmentation ratio, and eviction churn counter so we can correlate.

maria: Action items:
- jun: run the two-step perf-suite and push instrumentation (ETA 4h)
- eva: implement ghost list prototype and deploy to canary (ETA 6h)
- adeel: tweak sampler config and add single-use TTL rule (ETA 2h)
- maria: monitor perf-ci and escalate if OOM rate > 5/hour

maria: thanks all, keep updates here. :thumbsup:
